chat.text: Welcome to the ONSEN meeting for IETF 127.

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text: Thanks Samir, this simplification in problem areas is much appreciated

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: you want feedback now (since you mention my name) or at the end of the session?

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text: Would observability/assurance be updating multiple models or just focus on the problem space and not YANG updates?

chat.author: Samier Barguil
chat.text: My general feeling is it can be expanded to multiple models

chat.author: Kris Lambrechts
chat.text: Right, my feeling is that that problem area is around updating YANG. The general problem space, e.g. how do you actually implement this, is for me part of the "Implementation guidance" area.

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: Good questions Dhruv. I would be happy already with agreed guidelines for some consistency, to start with

chat.author: Qin Wu
chat.text: I feel it overlaps with what NMOP is doing.

chat.author: Michael Mackey
chat.text: The final slide from Ian showed there is overlap in a few areas

chat.author: Ian Farrer
chat.text: On the future work slide? I think there probably are - the items listed there are things people have raised, but we're not currently accepting as ONSEN work. If it's happening somewhere else then ONSEN won't take it

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: @Oscar or @Benoit - do you have suggested guidelines for consistency?

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: @Sue, I will have to do a little bit of homework before the guidelines: highlighting the discrepancies, and see what works.

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text: :plus:

chat.author: Fengchao FU
chat.text: Sounds good.  We will    think about it.

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: The left picture is exactly the SAIN architecture.

chat.author: Reshad Rahman
chat.text: @Benoit I was going to ask how this compares to SAIN...

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: Or the MEF Architecture.

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: SAIN = your decompose a service instance into smaller intents, which you verify independently.

chat.author: Oscar de Dios
chat.text: @Benoit, I belive the Network Models (not the service) which represent how the service is in the network is the link to the SAIN graph ....

chat.author: Chongfeng Xie
chat.text: Kris,  My question is about the scope of the "service" you mentioned. Based on my experience, operators' service includes computing as well as network connectivity, that is, it is a composite service. I wonder whether the orchestration here will consider attributes beyond network ?connectivity?

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: @Benoit - are the small intents that make SAIN flexible to request combination or parallel intents?

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: @sue, for ex, see figure 1 of RFC9417

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: @Cancun and @Chongfeng, thanks for putting together a CI/CD pipeline in place. It is probably a first. I had two comments. You may have noticed that not all the layers were going to be YANG and may be interconnected using NETCONF or RESTCONF. Hope your framework accounts for that? Also, are you making this available in GitHub publicly. Chongfeng, you seemed to have indicated that it will exported eventually. I would encourage it to be exposed publicly to begin with rather than wait.

chat.author: Joe Clarke
chat.text: Interesting work.  Is there a prelim check to see which modules can be passed through directly?

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: @benoit - RFC9417 diagram aligns with my point.

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: @Kris and team. Many thanks for this experiment: well done!

chat.author: Chongfeng Xie
chat.text: Mahesh, thank you for your suggestion. We will consider the issue you mentioned. Yes, we will export it to the Github and expose it publicly.

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: +1 to Benoit's comment.

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: +1 on thanks for experiment.

chat.author: Kris Lambrechts
chat.text: @ Chongfeng Yes, we are also considering non-YANG modelled components which could be brought in using the concepts briefly covered in the 2nd to last slide on non-YANG devices, which may include say cloud services.

chat.author: Oscar de Dios
chat.text: Thanks for the experiment. Just FYI, I did a few years back the mapping of Openconfig to Vendor Yangs. Even though , and while a good percentage was feasible... it turned out that from service model to "standard" device -> propietary was NOT usable for the real services , so the outcome was that the SM - NM - Propietary (or standard NATIVE) worked...

chat.author: Oscar de Dios
chat.text: said that.. sometimes you need "intermediate abstractions"... (and hence ONSEN :) )
